title: Frequency-dependent electron-phonon coupling and vibrational responses in tight-binding and continuous Dirac models with nuclear velocity correction
authors: Paolo Fachin, Francesco Macheda, Paolo Barone, Francesco Mauri
abstract: The nuclear motion induces in the electronic atomic orbitals a nuclear-velocity-dependent phase (also known as electron-translation factor), which modifies the effective Hamiltonians constructed from localised atomic orbitals. In this work, using an Ehrenfest Lagrangian approach for the localised atomic orbitals (LCAO) and tight-binding methods, we determine, at any order in the nuclear velocity, the equations of motion and the vibrational responses within a linear response formalism, focusing on the tight-binding assessment of the Born effective charges and the force-constant matrix. The appearance of nuclear-velocity-dependent Peierls-like phases in the non-local part of the interactions restores the all-electron sum rules for frequency-dependent vibrational responses. In tight-binding models these corrections crucially modify the vibrational response from a qualitative point of view, also yielding contributions required to capture phenomena such as vibrational circular dichroism. We test these corrections in the tight-binding model for metallic gapped graphene - finding excellent agreement with \textit{ab initio} calculations - and for the topological time-reversal symmetry breaking Haldane model.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to calculate vibrational responses in solids by incorporating the effect of nuclear motion on electron orbitals, treating it via an Ehrenfest Lagrangian approach. By including velocity-dependent phases, the authors restore fundamental physical sum rules that are otherwise violated in simpler tight-binding models. This is crucial for accurately predicting phenomena like vibrational circular dichroism.
main_problem: The work addresses determining frequency-dependent electron-phonon coupling and vibrational responses by accurately accounting for the nuclear velocity dependence of electronic atomic orbitals.
main_result: Including these nuclear velocity corrections restores fundamental all-electron sum rules for vibrational responses, providing crucial quantitative and qualitative improvements over standard tight-binding approximations.
method: The authors employ an Ehrenfest Lagrangian approach combined with tight-binding methods to derive the equations of motion and calculate vibrational responses within a linear response formalism.
model_or_system: The theory is applied using localized atomic orbitals (LCAO) and tested on condensed matter models such as graphene and the topological Haldane model, which are treated via effective Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Born effective charges, force-constant matrix, frequency-dependent vibrational responses, and contributions to vibrational circular dichroism.
important_parameters: Nuclear velocity ($\dot{\mathbf{R}}_s$) and its higher derivatives (acceleration $\ddot{\mathbf{R}}_s$), which are treated perturbatively up to any order.
main_assumptions: The derivation uses a semiclassical treatment where nuclei are classical, and the method assumes neglecting Stark effect mixing contributions in certain sections.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the velocity-dependent basis set using an Ehrenfest Lagrangian approach for LCAO, deriving generalized equations of motion incorporating nuclear velocity/acceleration terms, and finally applying this formalism to calculate vibrational responses and test it on specific models.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics (phonons), the rigorous derivation involving time-dependent Hamiltonians and coupling between electronic states and classical nuclear coordinates shares methodological parallels with open quantum systems dynamics where environment coupling is crucial.
